motion.$description: How long a change takes and how it moves. A transition reads one duration and one easing, as in transition: translate var(--motion-duration-base) var(--motion-easing-move). A transition that moves something reads base or slow, never fast, so the reduced-motion preference reaches it.

fast.$description: A change of colour or opacity, where nothing travels, such as a button's fill under the pointer. Reduced motion keeps it, so fades stay.

base.$description: A small movement, such as a card lifting a little under the pointer. Reduced motion makes it 0ms.

slow.$description: A large movement, such as a panel sliding in. Reduced motion makes it 0ms.

enter.$description: Something coming onto the screen: it arrives quickly and slows to a stop.

exit.$description: Something leaving the screen: it starts slowly and speeds away.

move.$description: Something that stays on screen as it changes, or moves from one place to another on it.
